dedupe_keys.name: crysys can traffic fabrication and masquerade benchmark

description: The CrySyS research team publishes Controller Area Network traffic for evaluating anomaly detection in vehicles. The deposit contains 26 benign recordings totalling more than 2.5 hours, together with traffic modified to represent fabrication and masquerade attacks. It is distributed as a ZIP package through Figshare under CC0 1.0 with free access. The collection page points to the specific dataset deposit, while a separate GPL-3.0 repository provides generation code and a sample CAN trace. Coverage is the recorded vehicle-network experiments, not a geographically representative traffic survey. The inspected own metadata does not state a complete calendar acquisition window or a uniform sampling interval. These logs can calibrate detection behaviour and compare cyber-disruption scenarios for connected vehicles or their digital twins. They complement general network simulation tools such as platform-ns-3, although no direct importer was verified. A caveat is that generated attacks reflect the authors' perturbation procedures and the available benign recordings. Performance on these traces alone does not establish resilience of an operational vehicle fleet.
